chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The father is not killed for his son, and the son is killed for his father; and a man does not inherit from another man when he kills him, even if it were in error.

key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: is killed/executed (for blood money or retaliation)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of execution and inheritance when a father kills his son or vice versa in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the asymmetry in capital punishment (qisas) and inheritance (mirath) between fathers and sons, reflecting the Shia juristic view that a father's life is not forfeited for his son's murder due to his superior status, whereas a son's is. It further establishes that homicide, whether intentional or accidental, severs the inheritance link, a principle derived from the Quranic verse 'And do not kill one another.'
